references.text: Both verses illustrate an ideal of faithful service where the servant has neither stolen nor damaged the master's property.
A theological contrast between Jacob's faithful keeping of sheep and God's complaint that Israel has not brought them as offerings.
The older son's argument in Luke mirrors Jacob's defense of his twenty years of faithful service to Laban.
Jacob's actual status as a 'foreigner' with Laban illustrates the theological truth in Leviticus that we are all sojourners with God.
A theological contrast between Jacob's respect for Laban's goats and God's independence from human sacrificial animals.
